# Story 41 — Agent assigns a ticket (Story: CRM-77)

> **Two corrections at review, both of which would have shipped a broken
> screen.**
>
> **1. There is no `GET /tickets/:id`.** The router serves `POST /tickets`,
> `GET /tickets`, `GET /ticket-categories`, `PATCH /tickets/:id/assignee` and
> `PATCH /tickets/:id/status` — and nothing else
> (`tickets.routes.js:14,20,37,50,63`). The plan below loads a ticket by id on
> mount; that request would 404. No story asks for a detail screen either, so
> there is no page to put one on.
>
> **Decision: assignment happens in the queue row, not on a detail page.** The
> queue already holds the ticket and its revision, which is everything the
> write needs. This keeps the story inside `web/` as its intake requires, and
> it is the better product besides — an agent assigns from the list they are
> looking at, rather than navigating into a screen that exists only to hold one
> control. Every acceptance criterion survives the move: the list of assignees,
> the option of nobody, the 409 that offers a reload, and holding the new
> revision so a second assignment from the same row is not refused.
>
> **2. A stale revision is `REVISION_MISMATCH`, not `CONFLICT`.** The service
> throws `new HttpError(409, 'REVISION_MISMATCH')`
> (`tickets.service.js:214`) — 409 is the status, the code is the domain's.
> Worse, `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts:5-13` does not list that code at all, so
> it falls through to `t.errors.INTERNAL` and a stale write currently reads as
> "something went wrong at our end". That is the exact failure this story's
> second criterion forbids, and fixing it means extending `ApiErrorCode` — see
> the new task 0 below.

### 0 — Teach the client the codes the API actually sends

**Files:** `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts`, `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts`, `ar.ts`

`ApiErrorCode` lists the eight base codes and stops. The API deliberately sends
domain codes at documented statuses — `errors.js:29-31` says so outright: "409
CONFLICT and 409 REVISION_MISMATCH are both honest answers". Three such codes
exist today, all of them 409s from the tickets feature:

- `REVISION_MISMATCH` — the revision sent was stale (this story reads it)
- `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION` — the status machine refuses the move (CRM-81 reads it)
- `STATUS_UNCHANGED` — the ticket already has that status (CRM-81 reads it)

Add all three to the union and a sentence for each to both resource files. The
`satisfies Record<ApiErrorCode, string>` on `t.errors` is what makes this worth
doing: with the code in the union, a missing sentence is a compile error rather
than a screen that silently says the wrong thing. All three are added now
rather than one per story, because the API sends all three now and the union is
supposed to describe the API rather than the screens built so far.

## Prerequisites

- **TICKETS-1-API** shipped: `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/:id/assignee` exists, validates the caller's revision, returns 409 on mismatch, and answers with the ticket at its new revision (BR-5).
- **IDENTITY-5-API** shipped: `GET /api/v1/assignees` returns the live staff list, paginated (`limit`/`offset`), and includes an "unassigned" option shape the API already documents.
- Read `.squad/plan-lessons.md` end-to-end before touching code. In particular L-30 (fetch stubs must build a fresh `Response` per call).
- No coordination with the API team is required for this story: **no `api/` file changes**.

## Story Goal

Give an agent a screen that assigns (or unassigns) a single ticket to a staff member picked from the API's live assignee list, honouring optimistic concurrency (BR-5) and keeping every visible string in the resource files (BR-6).

Concrete outcomes:

1. The assignee dropdown is populated from `GET /api/v1/assignees` and includes a first-class **"Unassigned"** option that sends `assigneeId: null`.
2. A successful `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/:id/assignee` updates the local ticket **and its `revision`** so a second assignment from the same screen is not refused.
3. A `409 CONFLICT` response is shown as a *"the ticket changed underneath you"* state with a **Reload** action, not as the generic error sentence.
4. Every rendered string comes from `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `ar.ts`; parity is preserved.

Explicitly out of scope: status change, priority change, resolution edits, bulk assign, notifications, any `api/` change. See "Out of scope" in the intake.

## Product rules (from story)

Current behaviour vs new:

- **Current:** the queue can show a ticket's assignee (read only). There is no screen that changes it.
- **New:** an agent can open an assign screen for a ticket, pick a staff member (or "Unassigned"), submit, and either see the updated ticket or a **stale-revision reload prompt**.

BR-5 (no silent overwrite) and BR-2 (every mutation audited) apply. BR-2 is enforced by the API and needs no web work; BR-5 is where this screen becomes visible.

## Implementation tasks

### 1 — Assignees data hook

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useAssignees.ts`

- Export a hook `useAssignees()` that calls `GET /assignees?limit=…&offset=…` via `request<AssigneePage>` from `web/src/shared/api/client.ts`, driven by `useRequest<AssigneePage>` from `web/src/shared/hooks`.
- Types:

```ts
export type Assignee = { id: string; name: string };
export type AssigneePage = { items: Assignee[]; total: number; limit: number; offset: number };
```

- Follow the shape of `useTicketQueue.ts` (lines 38–87): trigger the fetch in a `useEffect` on mount, expose `{ status, error, page, reload }`.
- **Pagination:** for MVP, request a single large-enough page (e.g. `limit=100`, `offset=0`). Do not build a scroller yet — the intake calls the endpoint "already paginated" but does not ask for infinite scroll here. If `page.total > page.items.length`, surface a muted note that only the first N are shown; add a `TODO` comment referencing the follow-up.
- Never mutate the returned array; treat it as read-only.

### 2 — Assign hook (the BR-5 core)

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useAssignTicket.ts`

- Export `useAssignTicket(ticketId: string)`.
- Internally uses two `useRequest` instances: one for the initial `GET /tickets/:id` load, one for the `PATCH /tickets/:id/assignee` submit.
- Types (mirror the queue's `Ticket` at `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts` lines 19–28, plus **`revision: number`**):

```ts
export type Ticket = {
  id: string;
  subject: string;
  status: string;
  priority: string;
  assigneeId: string | null;
  categoryId: string | null;
  revision: number;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
};
```

- On mount, `run(() => request<Ticket>(\`/tickets/${ticketId}\`))`. Keep the result as the "current ticket".
- Expose `assign(assigneeId: string | null): Promise<void>`. Internally:

```ts
await run(() =>
  request<Ticket>(`/tickets/${ticketId}/assignee`, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    body: JSON.stringify({ assigneeId, revision: current.revision }),
  }),
);
```

- **Hold the returned revision.** On success, set the local `ticket` to the response so the next call carries the new `revision`. This is acceptance criterion 3 of the intake ("a second assignment from the same screen must not be refused").
- Expose `reload()` that re-runs the `GET` — used by the 409 handler and the manual retry.
- Do **not** attempt to distinguish "stale" from other errors here; let the page read `error.code === 'REVISION_MISMATCH'` *(corrected — see the note at the top)*.

### 3 — Assign page

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/tickets/AssignTicketPage.tsx`

Follow `CustomersPage.tsx` (lines 31–153) and `TicketQueuePage.tsx` (lines 74–229) for structure. Use `Stack`, `Heading`, `Field`, `Select`, `Button`, `Skeleton`, `ErrorState`, `Card`, `Text` from `web/src/shared/ui`.

Layout:

1. `useParams<{ id: string }>()` for the ticket id.
2. Instantiate `useAssignees()` and `useAssignTicket(id)`.
3. Local state: `const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string>('')` seeded from the loaded ticket's `assigneeId` (empty string means "not yet chosen"; the special value for unassign is a constant, see below).
4. `const UNASSIGN_VALUE = 'unassigned'` — a page-local sentinel. **Do not** reuse `useTicketQueue.UNASSIGNED = 'none'` for the write path: the wire value is `null`, not `'none'`. Add a comment saying so.
5. Loading of the ticket → `<Skeleton …>`. Loading of the assignees → `<Skeleton …>` inside the field. Either fails → `<ErrorState>` keyed on `error.code`.
6. Success:
   - `<Field id="assignee-picker" label={t.ticketAssign.assigneeLabel}>` containing a `<Select>` whose options are:
     - `<option value="" disabled>{t.ticketAssign.choosePrompt}</option>` if nothing is selected.
     - `<option value={UNASSIGN_VALUE}>{t.ticketAssign.unassigned}</option>` — the **explicit** "return to nobody" choice.
     - One `<option value={a.id}>{a.name}</option>` per assignee from the page.
   - A submit button `t.ticketAssign.submit`, disabled while `assign.status === 'loading'` or while `selected === ''` or while `selected` still equals the ticket's current assignee representation.
7. On submit:

```ts
const assigneeId = selected === UNASSIGN_VALUE ? null : selected;
await assign(assigneeId).catch(() => {});
```

Do not clear `selected` on success; leave the picker showing the newly-assigned person so the agent can see the outcome without a re-read.

8. **409 handling — the point of the story.** When `assign.status === 'error' && assign.error?.code === 'CONFLICT'`, render a **distinct** `<ErrorState>` (or a `<Card>` with `ErrorState`-style content):
   - `title={t.ticketAssign.staleTitle}` — a title that says the ticket changed.
   - `body={t.ticketAssign.staleBody}` — a body that says the only useful next action is to reload.
   - `onRetry={() => { reload(); }}` with `retryLabel={t.ticketAssign.reload}`.
   - *(corrected)* The condition is `assign.error?.code === 'REVISION_MISMATCH'`.
     Reloading here means re-reading the queue, since there is no route that
     reads one ticket.
   - Do **not** fall through to `t.errors[error.code]` for a 409; that would collapse the code's meaning into the generic sentence. Explicitly branch on `CONFLICT` first, then fall through to the generic `t.errors[error.code] ?? t.errors.INTERNAL` for everything else.
9. Success confirmation: a muted `<Text>` line like `t.ticketAssign.assignedTo` interpolated with the assignee's display name (or `t.ticketAssign.unassignedConfirmation` when null). Interpolation is JS-side; **do not** embed variable text in a translation key value.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Same-person re-assign:** if `selected` resolves to the same wire value as the loaded ticket's `assigneeId`, disable the submit button. Prevents an obvious no-op PATCH that would still cost a network round trip. Enforced in `AssignTicketPage.tsx`.
- **Assign to nobody:** `selected === UNASSIGN_VALUE` sends `{ assigneeId: null, revision }`. A **missing** `assigneeId` would be a 422 from the API (intake calls this out) — never send `undefined`.
- **Stale revision (409):** page branches on `error.code === 'CONFLICT'` before the generic error path. Retry action calls `reload()` (the `GET`), which refreshes both the ticket **and its revision**. After a successful reload, `assign.status` returns to `idle` (via `useRequest`'s `reset()` or a fresh `run`); the picker is re-seeded from the reloaded ticket's `assigneeId`.
- **Second assignment from the same screen:** covered by `useAssignTicket` replacing the local ticket with the PATCH response body (which carries the new revision). Test explicitly.
- **Slow first request finishing after a fast second:** already handled by `useRequest`'s `latest` ticket (see `useRequest.ts` lines 13, 23, 35, 46). Do not add a second guard.
- **Empty assignees page:** show `t.ticketAssign.noAssignees` and keep the "Unassigned" option available; the submit button stays disabled unless `selected === UNASSIGN_VALUE`.
- **Assignees fetch fails:** page shows an `ErrorState` for the picker area, but a still-loaded ticket remains visible. Do not block the whole page.
- **Ticket fetch fails:** page shows a full-page `ErrorState` with retry; the picker is not rendered.
- **401 mid-session:** the shared `client.ts` (lines 76–82) already routes 401 through the unauthenticated handler. Nothing to do here.
- **Non-`ApiError` thrown from `fetch`:** `useRequest` (lines 28–34) normalises to `ApiError({ code: 'INTERNAL' })`; the page's generic branch handles it.
- **Route hit with a non-existent id:** API answers 404; page shows an `ErrorState` keyed on `t.errors.NOT_FOUND`.

## Test Plan

Add tests using Vitest + Testing Library. Follow the idiom in `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.test.tsx` and `web/src/pages/tickets/RaiseTicketPage.test.tsx`.

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/tickets/AssignTicketPage.test.tsx`

1. **Loads the ticket and the assignee list on mount.** Stub `fetch` to answer `GET /tickets/:id` and `GET /assignees` with distinct payloads (build a **fresh `Response` per call** — see plan-lessons L-30). Assert both requests fired and the picker options include every assignee **plus** the "Unassigned" option.
2. **Includes an explicit "Unassigned" option.** Assert it is present as a separate option from the "choose one" placeholder.
3. **Submits an assignment with the loaded revision.** Select an assignee, click submit. Assert the `PATCH` body was `{ assigneeId: '<id>', revision: <loaded revision> }`.
4. **Holds the new revision after success.** Prime the PATCH response with a ticket whose `revision` is loadedRevision+1. Submit again with a different assignee; assert the second PATCH body carries the **new** revision, not the original one. Both PATCHes must resolve without a 409. *(This is acceptance criterion 3 verbatim.)*
5. **Submits `null` for Unassigned.** Choose the "Unassigned" option, submit; assert body is `{ assigneeId: null, revision: … }` — literal `null`, not `'none'`, not omitted.
6. **On 409, shows the stale-ticket panel with a Reload action.** Stub `PATCH` to answer 409 with `{ code: 'CONFLICT' }`. Assert the rendered text is `t.ticketAssign.staleTitle` / `staleBody` (English test) — **not** the generic `t.errors.CONFLICT`. Click Reload; assert `GET /tickets/:id` fires again.
7. **After reload, the picker is re-seeded and a fresh submit sends the new revision.** Chain 409 → reload (returns ticket with newer revision) → submit → assert PATCH carries the reloaded revision.
8. **Same-person re-assign is disabled.** Selecting the currently-assigned person leaves the submit button disabled.
9. **Non-409 errors fall through to the generic error body.** Stub PATCH with `{ code: 'INTERNAL' }` 500; assert the body is `t.errors.INTERNAL`, and no Reload action is offered.

**Modify:**

10. `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` — no code change; it will fail automatically if `en.ts` and `ar.ts` diverge. Confirm it passes.
11. `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — no code change; confirm it still passes after adding the new page.
12. `web/src/app/routing.test.tsx` — add a case that navigating to `/tickets/:id/assign` renders the new page under auth.

**Do not** add API-side tests; this story ships no `api/` changes.
